summary: OpenAI introduces GeneBench-Pro, a 129-question research-level benchmark testing AI agents' scientific judgment in computational biology, and reports current frontier model pass rates on it.

mechanisms.reason: The results show pass rate scaling with reasoning-level test-time compute, indicating reasoning models spend more compute per query to improve performance.
mechanisms.quote: The results also show the impact of scaling test-time compute.

mechanisms.reason: A newer model solves far more problems while using fewer tokens than its predecessor, indicating a reduction in work required per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: At the highest reasoning level, GPT‑5.6 Sol solves nearly six times as many questions as GPT‑5.2 does while using about two-thirds as many tokens.

practices.reason: The lab publishes a deterministic, synthetically-grounded benchmark methodology and open-sources a subset of questions that an engineering team could run against its own models to measure judgment-heavy scientific reasoning.
practices.quote: We are fully open-sourcing 10 representative GeneBench-Pro questions on Hugging Face , with an interactive web interface for browsing them.
